subject: Does Stan have functionality for Bayesian Optimization?

messages.author: 8c3e0c4226a5e3e2
messages.subject: Does Stan have functionality for Bayesian Optimization?
parts:
I wanted to inquire whether Stan has functionality for Bayesian Optimization, as a tool for automatic model & parameter selection. (as described in this paper) . There are software tools for this in python, Java & C++. However, when I searched for any existing R packages, I found this one: rBayesianOptimization (https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/rBayesianOptimization/rBayesianOptimization.pdf). It cites Prof. Adam's paper from Harvard (https://arxiv.org/abs/1206.2944)

Thanks,
-- Daniel

messages.author: f13fe7e880ed6103
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Does Stan have functionality for Bayesian Optimization?
parts:
Hi Daniel. The answer, as far as I'm aware is no, but just to get a
sense of how hard it'd be to do, what are you imagining:

1) using Stan as the workhorse for doing the Gaussian process
regression on which Bayesian Optimization relies? or...

2) Are you hoping to write a model in Stan and then optimize it using
Bayesian Optimization instead of, say, BFGS?

For (1), Stan does GPs (see examples in manual), so you could
certainly consider replacing whatever GP implementation
rBayesianOptimization uses with a Stan-based approach. Or just writing
your own thing entirely. For (2), you can access the likelihood of a
Stan program in R, so you could probably wrap rBayesianOptimization
around it. (I have a project that hasn't gotten off the ground yet to
do this--actually Bayesian Optimization + Bayesian Quadrature--and
also use the gradient information that Stan provides for speeding up
the optimization, since you can put that into your GP as well. If
anyone is interested let me know...)

Seth
P.S. Nothing special about R/rBayesianOptimization in these
examples--the python BO packages are better developed.

On Saturday, October 8, 2016 at 1:40:57 AM UTC-7, Seth Flaxman wrote:
Hi Daniel. The answer, as far as I'm aware is no, but just to get a
sense of how hard it'd be to do, what are you imagining:

1) using Stan as the workhorse for doing the Gaussian process
regression on which Bayesian Optimization relies? or...

2) Are you hoping to write a model in Stan and then optimize it using
Bayesian Optimization instead of, say, BFGS?

I think it's (1). Since Gaussian Processes are a workhorse of Bayesian Optimization, I could use Stan to fit the GP.
But then I would need an implementation in Stan for the Expected Improvement (EI) algorithm, to select evaluation points for my "Acquisition function". (as described in this paper: https://arxiv.org/pdf/1206.2944.pdf)

For (1), Stan does GPs (see examples in manual), so you could
certainly consider replacing whatever GP implementation
rBayesianOptimization uses with a Stan-based approach. Or just writing
your own thing entirely. For (2), you can access the likelihood of a
Stan program in R, so you could probably wrap rBayesianOptimization
around it. (I have a project that hasn't gotten off the ground yet to
do this--actually Bayesian Optimization + Bayesian Quadrature--and
also use the gradient information that Stan provides for speeding up
the optimization, since you can put that into your GP as well. If
anyone is interested let me know...)

Seth
P.S. Nothing special about R/rBayesianOptimization in these
examples--the python BO packages are better developed.

messages.author: f13fe7e880ed6103
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Does Stan have functionality for Bayesian Optimization?
parts:
Couldn't you implement EI in R after running Stan to fit the GP? Once
you've fit a GP model in Stan you can make predictions at new points
in R using the samples.

Note that there's still the issue of how you actually pick the new
possible locations at which you evaluate EI. I asked about that here:
http://stats.stackexchange.com/questions/194166/practical-implementation-detail-of-bayesian-optimization
